c9e3f9aab_attacker_service_has_many_slot.meaning: attacker created a service with many slots for the purpose of the attack
c9e3f9aab_attacker_service_has_many_slot.checkpoint: before registration of victim address as instance
c9e3f9aab_attacker_service_has_many_slot.evidence: An attacker can create a service with many slots just for this purpose. This attack cannot be stopped by pausing the `ServiceManager` as there is not pause check in the `ServiceManager.registerAgents` function.

c9e3f9aab_service_in_active_registration.meaning: service is kept at ActiveRegistration state to register instances without intent to deploy
c9e3f9aab_service_in_active_registration.checkpoint: before registration of victim address as instance
c9e3f9aab_service_in_active_registration.evidence: The operator whitelist too is not helpful in this case as it is per service not global. So if the attacker creates his service, the whitelist won't help. The service can be created without the intention to push it to deploy but only to keep it at `ActiveRegistration` state just to be able to register instances and DOS other operators.

c9e3f9aab_victim_is_operator_address.meaning: the victim's address is an operator address used to register agent instances
c9e3f9aab_victim_is_operator_address.checkpoint: before registration of victim address as instance
c9e3f9aab_victim_is_operator_address.evidence: Neither the `ServiceManager.registerAgents` nor `ServiceRegistry.registerAgents` functions check whether the given instances addresses are already in use as operator address. So if a malicious operator uses another operator's address as an instance address while registering agent instances for a service, it will permanently block the other operator from registering any agent instance for any service in the future.

c9e3f9aab_operator_registered_instance_c.meaning: number of registered agent instances mapped to the operator address
c9e3f9aab_operator_registered_instance_c.checkpoint: while operator address is in use as operator
c9e3f9aab_operator_registered_instance_c.evidence: Add a mapping in `ServiceManager` contract to keep track of all operator addresses so that it will be checked when calling `ServiceManager.registerAgents` if any of the provided instances address is already an operator address. At the end of the function (meaning registration successful), add the operator address to the mapping by mapping it with the number of registered instances. During `ServiceManager.unbond`, reduce the mapped number of registered instances so that when 0, the address can be used as an instance address later.
